content:
When Apple finally responded to the significant increase in memory and other component costs, it showed no mercy. Some price hikes exceeded 50%, while memory and storage upgrades in some cases doubled outright.

These higher prices are very likely to persist for years, and may even be permanent...

9to5Mac readers were already skeptical about whether Apple would reduce prices once the component shortage eased. More than two-thirds of readers said they expected the price increases to be permanent.

A subsequent analyst report noted that supply chain pricing would not see any improvement before 2028, and even when conditions eased then, the effect would be quite limited. As it stands, today's extremely high pricing will likely last for years at minimum, and may never return to previous levels.

If this is indeed the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue buying Apple products at the same pace? Would you reduce the number or frequency of Apple purchases? Or would you take other measures, such as buying cheaper models, choosing refurbished units, or waiting for price drops before making a move?

Please take part in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments. The poll allows multiple selections, in case you plan to change your spending habits in more than one way.
